sections.title: From the garage sales to AGF

items.title: Obsessed with finding speakers
items.body: Garage sales, friends' houses. The acoustic-rendering concept sparked by his grandfather — "the first guy in Winnipeg to own stereo sound."

items.title: Inherited two massive Hi-Fi magazine collections
items.body: Bought & sold equipment to fund rent in teens.

items.title: Pawn-shop trading
items.body: Bought/sold professionally via pawn shops — brands and products pressure-tested in secondary markets. The first place the hallmarks of 'classics' become visible.
items.tag: Learned to read the market the way an analyst reads a P&L.

items.title: Professional recording in Toronto
items.body: Music, ADR, foley, sound-effects editing. First wave of chip-amp designers. SOTA software (WaveFrame, Pyramix 32-bit/384kHz). Hollywood mixing theaters alongside Roland TV stereo monitors.
items.tag: Direct exposure to both the high-art and the everyday-mass tiers in the same week.

items.title: First audio-tech startup
items.body: Father-in-law David Jaeger (world-famous cost-no-object live music recordings for public broadcasters) + David "Stretch" Quinney (THE mixing/mastering engineer) on Bryston-powered monitors in CBC Studio One. 13 Amps per stereo channel. BBC, Radio France, Radio Scotland rented the room for the Davids.

items.title: Mogulus — first live broadcast
items.body: Inspired the work with Justin Kan. Only platform with codec support for CD-quality live streaming of classical music — the first target, for a variety of reasons.
items.tag: Mogulus (later context: Justin.tv → Twitch via Justin Kan) ·

items.title: First tech-founder mentor
items.body: Alan Simmons, founder/CEO of V3 Semiconductor (Canada's first successful semi co., sold to National). Fostered product-definition talent, set loose on supply chain.

items.title: NMI Devices
items.body:
What Sonos became, architecturally. One of the first teams in the world to test-drive D2-Audio's DSP-driven amplification (Chip Taylor, famous pro-gear engineer). IP still an opportunity in 2026 — the foundation of Mark Levinson's "custom chip" marketing angle for his new brand.

**Outcome:** Shuttered after rejection by big Japanese brands ("digital amp will never sound good, who'd network their music anyway").

items.title: Mass Fidelity · Core · Relay
items.body: The first commercially successful deployment of Wave Field Synthesis. The Relay PR tour (291% over plan). Munich High-End. The Burmester conversation. The "you seem to have figured out some details we haven't" moment.
items.tag: Mass Fidelity · The proof of every tenet in real-world operation.

items.title: Dolby skunkworks
items.body: The "make things no one can get mad at us for" charter. Remora — the soundbar that lived behind the TV. The architecture that made it acoustically advantaged. The product Apple shut down via the licensing threat.

items.title: Watches the consolidation happen
items.body: Krell closes (Jun 2024). Samsung/Harman closes Sound United (Sep 2025). Barco closes VerVent (Apr 2026). Marshall now 78% HSG. The market-rhyme thesis inverts from prediction to observation.

items.title: AGF founded
items.body: The gospel, distilled. The plan, on the page.
items.tag: AGF — All Grounds Floating · AGF is the next move.
